content.text:
I've fixed the log lines bleeding into the TUI. Typecheck and the full test suite pass (364 tests, including 2 new ones). I haven't tried it in the actual Pi TUI, so `pi -e .` is the last thing to check on your side. Nothing is committed yet.

**Cause:** the logs come from LiteRT, the native C++ library inside `@desert-ant-labs/redact`. The first time the model runs, it writes those `INFO:`/`WARNING:` lines straight to stderr from native code. Node's `process.stderr` never sees them, so Pi can't catch or route them, and they land on top of the screen. I checked the library for a setting to turn the logging down and there isn't one.

**Fix:**
- **`src/services/native-stderr.ts`** (new): `withSilencedNativeStderr(fn)` points the process's stderr at `/dev/null` while `fn` runs, then puts it back. If two calls overlap, the redirect is only undone when the last one finishes. Where the redirect isn't possible (Windows, or the `koffi` library that makes the system calls missing), it just runs `fn` normally.
- **`src/services/redactor.ts`**: the model now loads and runs one throwaway pass (`"warm up"`) inside that wrapper, so all of LiteRT's setup logging happens while stderr is muted. If the warm-up fails, the model is closed and the error is passed on.
- **`package.json`**: `koffi` is now a direct dependency. It was already installed as an optional dependency of the redact package, but relying on that is fragile.
- **Opt-out:** setting `PI_PII_REDACT_NATIVE_LOGS=1` keeps the native logs, for debugging.
- **`tests/native-stderr.test.ts`**: runs the real model in a separate Node process and checks its raw stderr. With the fix, no LiteRT lines appear and normal stderr output works again afterwards. With the opt-out set, the logs do appear, which shows the test can catch the bug.
- I added a patch changeset, `.changeset/quiet-litert-logs.md`.

**Trade-off:** the mute covers the whole process for the second or so the model takes to load (on first use and again after a session restart). Anything else written to stderr in that window, including real native warnings, is lost too. Errors from loading still come through as normal JavaScript errors, so failures aren't hidden.

The `package-lock.json` diff also changes its version from 0.2.0 to 0.3.0. The lockfile was out of date and `npm install` brought it in line with `package.json`.

In our case, the issue is not limited to the Python package.

We are embedding LiteRT into a native C++ console application, and there currently appears to be no straightforward way to suppress or adjust the verbosity of INFO-level messages there either.

This makes integration more difficult because LiteRT logs are mixed with the application's own console output, making it harder to present clean logs to users or implement custom logging policies.

content.text:
That issue describes the proper fix, but neither of its suggestions can be reached from this extension, so the stderr redirect is still needed for now.

The issue offers two ways to lower LiteRT's log level:

1. **Call `LiteRtSetMinLoggerSeverity(LiteRtGetDefaultLogger(), ...)`.** I tried looking up both functions in the LiteRT library bundled with `@desert-ant-labs/redact` (and in its `libRedactNode.so`), and neither is exported. Calls like `LiteRtCreateEnvironment` are exported, so the build just doesn't include the logger calls.
2. **Pass a log level when creating the environment (`Environment::Create`).** The environment is created inside Desert Ant's compiled core, not by our code. The only option it reads from outside is `DAL_LITERT_THREADS`, so we can't pass a log level through.

Even with the API available, the last comment on the issue says it doesn't silence `INFO: Created TensorFlow Lite XNNPACK delegate for CPU.` Our logs include that line too, so it would still reach the TUI.

The right long-term fix belongs in `@desert-ant-labs/redact`. Their core should set LiteRT's minimum log level to warning or error when it creates the environment, or let callers pass a log level through `Redact.load()`. Once that ships we could drop the redirect, or keep it only for the XNNPACK line. I can draft an issue for their repo that links LiteRT #7420 and includes the log output we saw.

cat > /tmp/issue.md <<'EOF'
## Summary

With `@desert-ant-labs/redact` 4.2.1 on Node (`/native`, linux-x64 and linux-arm64), LiteRT writes its INFO/WARNING setup logs straight to file descriptor 2 the first time `redaction()` runs. These writes come from native code, so they skip `process.stderr` and the host app can't intercept them. In a terminal UI (we embed the library in a [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) extension, `@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact`) the lines land on top of the rendered screen.

```
INFO: [environment.cc:36] Creating LiteRT environment with options
WARNING: [npu_registry.cc:34] NPU accelerator could not be loaded and registered: kLiteRtStatusErrorInvalidArgument.
INFO: [gpu_registry.cc:101] Attempting to load GPU accelerator(libLiteRtGpuAccelerator.so).
INFO: [gpu_registry.cc:101] Attempting to load GPU accelerator(libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so).
INFO: [gpu_registry.cc:101] Attempting to load GPU accelerator(libLiteRtOpenClAccelerator.so).
INFO: [gpu_registry.cc:101] Attempting to load GPU accelerator(libLiteRtVulkanAccelerator.so).
WARNING: [gpu_registry.cc:131] GPU accelerator could not be loaded and registered.
INFO: [accelerator_registry.cc:54] RegisterAccelerator: ptr=0x..., name=CpuAccelerator
INFO: [cpu_registry.cc:75] XNNPACK CPU accelerator registered.
INFO: [compiled_model.cc:833] Flatbuffer model initialized directly from incoming litert model.
INFO: Created TensorFlow Lite XNNPACK delegate for CPU.
```

## Reproduce

```js
import { Redact } from "@desert-ant-labs/redact/native";
const r = await Redact.load();                       // silent
await r.redaction("Email john@example.com please");  // the log lines above go to stderr
```

## Why callers can't fix this

LiteRT has an API for this (see google-ai-edge/LiteRT#7420): `LiteRtSetMinLoggerSeverity(LiteRtGetDefaultLogger(), ...)`, or a log level passed when the environment is created. Neither is reachable from callers of this package:

- The bundled `libLiteRt.so` doesn't export `LiteRtSetMinLoggerSeverity` or `LiteRtGetDefaultLogger` (`LiteRtCreateEnvironment` and similar are exported).
- The LiteRT environment is created inside the native core. As far as we can tell, the only option it reads from outside is `DAL_LITERT_THREADS`.

For now we work around it by pointing fd 2 at `/dev/null` (with `dup`/`dup2` via koffi) while we load the model and run a warm-up pass. That also hides any other stderr output from the process during that window, so we'd rather not keep it.

## Request

Any of these would solve it:

1. Have the core set LiteRT's minimum log severity to WARNING or ERROR by default when it creates the environment. Per the LiteRT issue, this can be done through the environment options or `LiteRtSetMinLoggerSeverity`.
2. Add a `logLevel` (or `quiet`) option to `LoadOptions` and/or an environment variable such as `DAL_LITERT_LOG_LEVEL`.
3. Export `LiteRtSetMinLoggerSeverity` / `LiteRtGetDefaultLogger` from the bundled `libLiteRt.so`, so callers can set the level through FFI.

Note: according to the LiteRT issue, `INFO: Created TensorFlow Lite XNNPACK delegate for CPU.` comes from TFLite's minimal logger and isn't covered by the LiteRT logger setting, so it may need separate handling.

## Environment

- `@desert-ant-labs/redact` 4.2.1, `@desert-ant-labs/core` 4.2.1, koffi 2.16.3
- Node 24.22.1, Linux arm64 (the same happens on x64)
EOF

I opened an issue in the redact library's repo: https://github.com/Desert-Ant-Labs/desert-ant-core/issues/247

It includes:
- **The problem:** LiteRT's setup logs go straight to stderr from native code on the first `redaction()` call, so they show up on top of TUI apps like Pi. It quotes the log lines we saw.
- **A short reproduction** using `Redact.load()` and `redaction()`.
- **Why callers can't fix it:** the bundled library doesn't export `LiteRtSetMinLoggerSeverity` or `LiteRtGetDefaultLogger`, and the LiteRT environment is created inside their core where we can't pass options. It links google-ai-edge/LiteRT#7420.
- **Our current workaround** (muting stderr while the model loads and warms up) and why we'd rather not keep it.
- **Three possible fixes:**
  - default the log level to warning or error;
  - add a `logLevel` option to `LoadOptions` or an environment variable;
  - export the LiteRT logger functions so callers can set the level themselves.
- **A note** that the `Created TensorFlow Lite XNNPACK delegate` line comes from a different logger and may need separate handling.
